name: ae studio plush snake
units: 1 unit = D, the outer diameter of the body with its fur

axes.pose: the "ae" pose of the client photo (assets/img/snake-ae.jpg)

mesh.uv0: u = arc length from the nose / L, v = angle around the body from the belly line (0..1)
others: EyeL, EyeR: glossy black beads (follow Head)

skeleton.root: Head (the chain runs nose -> tail tip)
skeleton.jaw: Jaw: child of Head, no skin weights yet

fur.direction: combed toward the tail with a parting along the side mid-lines; on the head it radiates from the snout
fur.shading: tips are a lighter tint of the strand colour; roots ~50 % darker on the body, not on the muzzle

animation.name: idle_lookaround
animation.content: breathing (2 breaths, ~2 % swell), head looks to one side, the other, a little up, back; two tongue flicks

camera.note: same camera as clip A (1280x720); the photo is 1408x768 with the same lens and pose

snake_albedo.webp.content: fur colour as seen: pink, cream bands with black edges, lighter head and muzzle, darker ring round the eyes

snake_normal.webp.content: tangent-space normal of soft pile bumps (glTF convention, +G = image up); use at low strength

fur_strands.webp.R: strand height / mask for shell alpha: the shell at height h (0..1) keeps texels with R >= h
fur_strands.webp.source: Cycles render of real hair curves seen from above

clipA.webm: snake_idle.webm: VP9 + alpha, the snake with its shadow, 1280x720
clipA.preview: snake_idle_preview.mp4: H.264 on the powder-pink backdrop
clipA.passes: PNG passes (rgba_####.png snake on transparent, shadow_####.png black shadow sprite) are kept locally
